title: Chennai 2015 Floods — City-wide Inundation
conditions: 3-day cumulative rainfall over 1000mm; reservoirs at full storage released simultaneously
outcomeSummary: Uncoordinated release of reservoir water compounded surface flooding; hospitals cut off for over 24 hours in worst-hit zones.
actionsTaken: Reactive evacuation after flooding was already citywide; no pre-emptive drainage staging.
lessonLearned: Reservoir release timing must be coordinated with drainage capacity forecasts, not decided independently by each authority.

title: Ward 18 Flash Flood & Hospital Road Paralysis
conditions: 115 mm/hr rain + 25% drain capacity + peak morning traffic
outcomeSummary: Mobile pumps deployed to Ward 18 in 2021, but risk was reduced only 8% because the storm drain outfall was already submerged by canal backflow — the pumps had nowhere to discharge to.
actionsTaken: Delayed manual pump deployment after flooding began; traffic police deployed manually with no signal pre-emption.
lessonLearned: Pump deployment is ineffective once the outfall is submerged — check outfall status before committing pump units, not just drain saturation.

title: Cyclone Michaung — Coastal Ward Storm Surge + Rainfall
location: Chennai coastal wards, incl. Ward 18 periphery
conditions: Very heavy rainfall (>200mm/day) combined with storm surge and sustained high winds
outcomeSummary: Airport and multiple hospital access roads flooded; power outages disabled traffic signals city-wide for 14+ hours, compounding gridlock during evacuation.
actionsTaken: Evacuation advisories issued only after flooding was visible on major roads; backup generators at 2 of 4 major hospitals failed.
lessonLearned: Power infrastructure stress must trigger traffic-signal contingency planning before outage occurs, not after — signal failure during evacuation is a compounding, not independent, risk.

title: Velachery Recurring Waterlogging — Pump Station Overload
conditions: Sustained 60-70mm/hr rainfall over 4 hours; single pump station serving the basin
outcomeSummary: Pump station load exceeded 90% and one of two units tripped on thermal overload after 3 hours of continuous operation; second unit alone could not keep pace with inflow.
actionsTaken: No load-balancing across pump stations; single station ran until failure instead of staged rotation.
lessonLearned: Pump stations need scheduled rotation/rest cycles under sustained load — running a single unit to failure is worse than staged rotation across available units.

title: Ward 18 Pre-emptive Pump Staging Drill — Successful
conditions: IMD heavy rainfall warning issued 6 hours ahead; 90mm/hr forecast
outcomeSummary: Mobile pumps staged at Station 4B two hours before rainfall onset, based on IMD nowcast. Drain saturation capped at 55% and road flooding was avoided entirely.
actionsTaken: Pre-emptive pump staging triggered by nowcast, not by observed flooding.
lessonLearned: Acting on the rainfall nowcast rather than waiting for drain saturation telemetry buys the lead time that makes pump deployment actually effective.

title: Hospital Road Green-Wave Signal Override — 2021
conditions: Traffic gridlock following the Nov 2021 flood; ambulance transit at risk
outcomeSummary: Green-wave signal override on Route B cleared the corridor for emergency transit within 8 minutes, cutting ambulance delay by roughly 35%.
actionsTaken: Traffic Bureau activated corridor override as soon as gridlock was flagged by Emergency Services, without waiting for a formal request.
lessonLearned: Cross-department triggers (Emergency flags -> Traffic acts) are faster than waiting for a sequential request chain.

title: Route Diversion Onto Already-Saturated Route — 2022
conditions: Moderate flooding; Traffic diverted vehicles to R9 without checking Water's saturation flag on that route
outcomeSummary: Traffic diverted the corridor onto R9, a route Water had already flagged as saturated from canal backflow; the diversion created a second gridlock point instead of relieving the first.
actionsTaken: Diversion decided by Traffic Bureau alone, without cross-checking Water's saturation data for the target route.
lessonLearned: A diversion target must be checked against every other department's flags before being adopted — this is the exact failure mode the conflict-detection step exists to catch.

title: Citizen Report Surge Preceding Ward 18 South Cluster
conditions: 38 geotagged citizen reports of waterlogging within 15 minutes, ahead of official telemetry confirmation
outcomeSummary: Citizen report clustering flagged the Ward 18 South waterlogging pocket roughly 20 minutes before drain sensors crossed threshold, giving responders extra lead time.
actionsTaken: Public advisory issued based on report cluster, ahead of telemetry confirmation.
lessonLearned: Citizen report volume is a legitimate leading indicator, not just a sentiment signal — it can arrive before instrumented telemetry.

title: Post-flood Water Supply Contamination — Ward 18
conditions: Sustained drain saturation above 80% for over an hour, canal backflow into low-lying supply lines
outcomeSummary: Sewage intrusion into the municipal supply line was only detected two days after the flood, during a routine quality check, forcing a boil-water advisory.
actionsTaken: No real-time contamination monitoring tied to drain saturation; detection was incidental.
lessonLearned: Sustained high drain saturation should trigger a proactive water-quality advisory, not wait for a scheduled test to catch it days later.

title: Cyclone Michaung — Low-Lying Ward Evacuation Order
conditions: Inundation exceeding 35cm in low-lying pockets during Cyclone Michaung
outcomeSummary: Evacuation advisory was issued on time, but power outage disabled the SMS gateway for 40 minutes, delaying reach to roughly a third of the target population.
actionsTaken: Single-channel (SMS) advisory dispatch with no fallback channel when power infrastructure is already under stress.
lessonLearned: Evacuation advisories need a channel that doesn't depend on the same power infrastructure the scenario is already stressing.

title: Ward 12 Synthetic Event — Moderate Rain, No Cascade
conditions: 55mm/hr rainfall, drains at design capacity, no pre-existing blockage
outcomeSummary: Rainfall stayed below the drain saturation threshold; no cascade occurred and no intervention was needed.
actionsTaken: None required — situation self-resolved within normal drainage capacity.
lessonLearned: Not every rainfall event needs a response — the non-linear threshold in the causal model reflects a real distinction, not just a modelling simplification.

title: Ward 18 Synthetic Event — Deferred Maintenance Pump Failure
conditions: Moderate rainfall (80mm/hr) but 3 of 4 mobile pumps found to have deferred maintenance ahead of the event
outcomeSummary: Despite only moderate rainfall, pre-existing pump maintenance deficits meant effective pump capacity was far below rated capacity, and road flooding occurred at a rainfall level that should have been manageable.
actionsTaken: Pumps deployed per standard protocol without checking maintenance status first.
lessonLearned: Rainfall intensity alone does not predict outcome — pre-existing infrastructure deficits (maintenance debt) can dominate the result independent of rainfall.

title: Substation Trip Cascading Into Signal Failure
conditions: Localized flooding reached a transformer bay; substation tripped as a safety measure
outcomeSummary: Automatic substation shutoff for safety cascaded into a 14-intersection signal outage, adding an estimated 40% to corridor congestion during an already-active response.
actionsTaken: No signal-failure contingency (manual traffic control) was pre-staged for this substation's service area.
lessonLearned: A power-outage risk above the automatic-shutoff threshold should pre-stage manual traffic control at dependent intersections, not react after signals go dark.

title: Ward 18 2021 Flood — Full Incident Retrospective
conditions: 115 mm/hr rain, 25% drain capacity, peak morning traffic, one ambulance carrying a critical patient
outcomeSummary: Overall response reduced projected risk by roughly 40%, but the single highest-cost failure was the pump/outfall mismatch (see HIST-2021-11-W18) — the traffic and emergency response components performed well in isolation.
actionsTaken: Mixed: traffic diversion and signal override succeeded; pump deployment underperformed due to outfall submersion.
lessonLearned: A coordinated response can still underperform if even one department's action targets the wrong constraint — partial success on 3 of 4 fronts is not the same as success.

title: Ward 9 Synthetic Event — Citizen Report Cluster, No Confirmed Flooding
conditions: 31 citizen reports within 15 minutes, but drain telemetry never crossed threshold
outcomeSummary: A public advisory was issued based on the citizen report cluster alone; it turned out to be a localized drainage grate blockage, not a ward-wide event, causing unnecessary alarm.
actionsTaken: Advisory issued from citizen reports without cross-checking drain telemetry or dispatching a field verification first.
lessonLearned: Citizen reports are a good leading indicator but should be corroborated with at least one other signal before triggering a public advisory, not acted on alone.
